sections.h2: Where is Fauquier County and what is it like?
sections.html:
Fauquier County sits on the Piedmont in Northern Virginia, about 651 square miles of mostly open country with Warrenton as the county seat. The 2020 census counted 72,972 residents, and the Census Bureau estimate for 2025 is 76,503.

The 2020 census counted 26,400 households and a median age of 41.9. Wikipedia calls the county not densely populated but notes that exurban development from the Washington area has reached parts of it, including housing complexes along highways in rural areas. The highest point is Blue Mountain at 2,208 feet on the northwestern border with Warren County.

sections.h2: Which Fauquier County communities do sellers come from?
sections.html:
Beyond the three towns, Fauquier has a string of unincorporated places that appear on mailing addresses and deeds. The census-designated places are Bealeton, Calverton, Catlett, Marshall, Midland, New Baltimore, Opal, Paris, Rectortown and Upperville.

New Baltimore is the largest community in the county, and Wikipedia ties recent growth to Warrenton and New Baltimore, with the Brookside and Vint Hill subdivisions feeding growth in the east. The census counted 57.5 percent of residents in rural areas in 2020, so land use rules, covered below, come up more here than in a city.

Warrenton and Remington run their own police departments, according to Wikipedia. The county sheriff covers the rest.

sections.h2: How do people get around Fauquier County?
sections.html:
Wikipedia lists Interstate 66 and five U.S. routes among the county's major highways.

  • Interstate and U.S. routes: I-66, US 15, US 17, US 29, US 50 and US 211.
  • State routes: SR 28, SR 55, SR 215, SR 245 and SR 355.
  • Neighbors: Loudoun, Prince William, Stafford, Culpeper, Rappahannock, Warren and Clarke counties.

Wikipedia reports that, as of the 2000 census, 47% of working residents had jobs outside the county, and average travel time to work was 39.2 minutes. Those are older figures, but they explain why many owners here treat the house as a base for a commute.

sections.h2: What do people do for work in Fauquier County?
sections.html:
Local government and health care lead. The county's 2023 financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, ranks the Fauquier County School Board first with 1,000 or more employees.

  1. Fauquier County School Board, 1,000 and over
  2. County of Fauquier, 500 to 999
  3. Fauquier Health System, 500 to 999
  4. U.S. Department of Transportation, 500 to 999
  5. Walmart, 250 to 499

The county is also known for horse country. The Virginia Gold Cup steeplechase has been held in Fauquier since 1922.

sections.h2: Which school districts and colleges serve Fauquier County?
sections.html:
Most of the county is in the Fauquier County Public Schools division. The part on Marine Corps Base Quantico falls under the Defense Department's school system instead.

High schools named on Wikipedia are Fauquier High School, Liberty High School and Kettle Run High School, and the division also runs Mountain Vista Governor's School. Laurel Ridge Community College is the local college. School boundaries can affect how a buyer sees a house, so keep the correct school name in your listing or offer paperwork.

sections.h2: What is the Fauquier County real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
The Commissioner of the Revenue's rate page shows a combined real estate rate of $0.895 per $100 of assessed value. That figure is $0.709 base, $0.182 for the fire and rescue levy and $0.004 for the conservation easement fund.

At $0.895, a house assessed at $500,000 would owe $4,475 a year, or $2,237.50 per half. That is simple arithmetic from the published rate, not a quote.

One special district appears: the Marshall Electric Light and Business Improvement district adds $0.025 per $100. Mobile homes are taxed at the same $0.895 as real estate. The rate page does not carry a date, so confirm the current-year figure with the office when you plan a sale.

sections.h2: When are Fauquier County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Fauquier bills half the year in June and half in December. The key tax dates list June 5 for the first half and December 5 for the second half, both paid to the Treasurer's Office, and any date that falls on a weekend moves to the next business day.

  • March 5: renewal for tax relief for the elderly, filed with the Commissioner of the Revenue.
  • June 5: first half real estate taxes due.
  • October 25: revalidation and new land use applications due.
  • December 5: second half real estate taxes due.

Payments and balances are handled through the county's online tax portal, and the Treasurer is Tanya Remson Wilcox. The pages reviewed did not state the late penalty, so ask the Treasurer's Office for the current penalty and interest before you let a bill slide.

sections.h2: How does Fauquier County reassess and hear appeals?
sections.html:
Fauquier reassesses every four years. The last reassessment took effect January 1, 2026, the process carries through 2027, and new values take effect January 1, 2028.

The county's Board of Equalization hears property assessment disputes. The Circuit Court appoints its five members, who must be county residents and a majority freeholders, with at least 30 percent drawn from appraisal, real estate, building, legal or financial work. The ordinance deadline to appeal to the 2026 board was June 17, 2026.

The Commissioner of the Revenue's office is at 10 Courthouse Square, 2nd Floor, Warrenton, VA 20186, phone (540) 422-8880. If the board's result is not enough, Virginia law lets a taxpayer apply to the circuit court. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 presumes the assessor's value, or the board's adjusted value, is correct and puts the burden on the taxpayer to show the value was wrong and not set under accepted appraisal practice.

sections.h2: What land use and tax relief programs affect a Fauquier sale?
sections.html:
Fauquier runs a use value program that taxes qualifying farm, forest, horticultural and open space land on its use instead of its market value. If the land stops qualifying, a roll-back assessment applies, and the county says it requires repayment of the deferred tax plus 10 percent interest for five years plus the current year.

That matters when you sell acreage. Ask the Commissioner of the Revenue whether the parcel is in land use before you agree to a closing date, since a change in use can trigger the bill.

The county also offers real estate tax relief for owners age 65 and older or permanently disabled, with reduction or exemption based on income and net worth, applied for each year. The office number for that program is 540-422-8140.

sections.h2: What happens to Fauquier County tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
The tax lien on a Virginia house outranks other liens until it is paid. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 says sale proceeds must be applied to taxes and levies on the real estate, including penalties and interest, and that the seller's share is prorated by contract.

On the recording side, a deed carries a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 under Virginia Code 58.1-802, paid by the seller unless the buyer agrees to cover it. The Commissioner's office says it keeps ownership records current from deed transfers and other records obtained from the Clerk of the Circuit Court, and asks for timely recording so the right owner is taxed.

faqs.q: What is the combined Fauquier County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's rate page lists $0.895 per $100 of assessed value, made up of $0.709 base, $0.182 fire and rescue and $0.004 conservation easement fund.

faqs.q: When is Fauquier County real estate tax due?
faqs.a: June 5 for the first half and December 5 for the second half, with weekend dates moving to the next business day.

faqs.q: When did Fauquier County last reassess property?
faqs.a: The last reassessment took effect January 1, 2026. New assessed values take effect January 1, 2028.

faqs.q: Who hears assessment appeals in Fauquier County?
faqs.a: The Board of Equalization, a five-member panel appointed by the Circuit Court, hears them. The ordinance deadline for the 2026 board was June 17, 2026.

faqs.q: Do I owe money back if my Fauquier land is in the use value program?
faqs.a: Possibly. A change from a qualifying use triggers a roll-back, which the county describes as the deferred tax plus 10 percent interest for five years plus the current year.
